$comment: Provenance for the curated Fashion artwork, so any of it can be swapped later
without redoing the detective work. Written by hand alongside the picks in
scripts/seed-tab-art.mjs; that file is what actually uploads, this one is what
records where each photograph came from and why it was chosen.
Every photo_page_url below was opened AT FULL SIZE before it was chosen. On this
project alt text has been wrong repeatedly - one candidate described as a stack of
caps turned out to be woven table mats - so nothing here was picked from a filename
or a description. The rejects, with the reason each one died, are in the header
comment of scripts/seed-tab-art.mjs rather than duplicated here.
storage_path is relative to the 'product-images' bucket on Supabase. The public URL
crop is what the file was baked to; a rect is in the ORIGINAL photograph's pixels
and is applied before the resize.
round: Fashion tab - lookbook circles (3) and the 'What are you looking for?' type tiles (7)

source_rules.licence: Licensed free stock only - Unsplash Licence or Pexels Licence. No Unsplash+ (paid): its download endpoint 403s, which is a licence gate.
source_rules.content: Real photography only, no AI-generated people. No visible third-party brand logos or wordmarks in frame. No baked-in text, watermarks or price tags. No image used twice, and none duplicating an image already in tabArt.ts, in apps/web/public/tiles/, or an existing product photograph.
source_rules.dedupe_check: Every id below was grepped against the whole repo - which is where every product-photo seed script AND apps/web/public/tiles/SOURCES.txt record their source ids - and against the existing tabArt.ts / seed-tab-art.mjs constants. Zero matches. That grep is not ceremony: it is what caught photo-1619603364937-8d7af41ef206, the best men's frame of this round, already shipped as apps/web/public/tiles/fashion-men-circle.jpg and still served through browse_tiles.
source_rules.crop_control: Unsplash honours `rect` (x,y,w,h in the ORIGINAL photograph's pixels, applied before the resize). PEXELS DOES NOT - it accepts w/h/fit=crop/fm and the named crop anchors, and silently ignores both `rect` and `crop=focalpoint`, returning 200 with the uncropped frame. The two Pexels slots below are therefore framed by the source photograph and take the centre box; seed-tab-art.mjs throws if a rect is ever added to one.

circles.$comment: CIRCLE_ART['fashion'] in apps/web/src/lib/tabArt.ts. Keys are the Fashion subcategory slugs. Rendered at ~80px, masked round. All 400x400 WebP. The 'Shop for' row is now THREE - women, men, kids-fashion, re-shot this round as one lookbook; bags/caps/belts/scarves stay in the map but have moved to the type-tile row and their entries are left below unchanged.
circles.$brief: Fashion-brand lookbook photography of the kind Zara / SHEIN / Trendyol use on category tiles: full styled outfit, considered lighting, clean or plain-toned background, cropped so the CLOTHES read at small circle size rather than the face. No busy backgrounds, no obvious stock-photo posing, no real brand logos. The three below were chosen as a ROW and judged side by side as 88px discs, which is where two individually-better frames lost.

women.shows: A woman in a deep aubergine satin shirt over ivory wide-leg trousers and silver strappy sandals, against a cream draped fabric backdrop in soft even light. Full styled outfit; the crop takes her from the chin to mid-calf, so the disc is the shirt and trousers rather than a portrait.
women.rect_reason: The source is a full-length 3858x5787 frame; centred, the square would be hips-to-ankles. This box starts at the chin and ends mid-calf so the garments fill the disc.

men.shows: A man in a camel wool overcoat over a burgundy roll-neck, navy trousers and black leather loafers, on a plain white studio ground. Full styled outfit head to toe in the source; the centre square lands on collar-to-knee, which is the coat.
men.no_rect_reason: Pexels ignores `rect`. This frame needs none - the centre box is already the coat.
men.checked: The only hardware on the coat is a small silver leaf-shaped pin on the lapel, opened at 6x magnification to confirm it is an ornament and not a wordmark.

kids-fashion.shows: A boy in a sage ribbed knit jumper and tan waffle joggers with white trainers, on white seamless. Styled kidswear from a studio lookbook shoot, not a candid snapshot - which is what the brief asked for.
kids-fashion.no_rect_reason: Pexels ignores `rect`, so this frame cannot be tightened.
kids-fashion.known_compromise: Its subject sits smaller in the disc than Women or Men, because the crop cannot be pulled in. The one kidswear photograph that COULD be tightened - Unsplash photo-1759313560181-de61e7235355, clean, no marks, outfit filling the frame - is on a saturated yellow seamless that broke the row of three. Both were rendered as 88px discs beside Women and Men before this was chosen; the row won over the single disc. Swap to that id if a louder Kids circle is ever wanted.

bags.shows: A tan canvas holdall - the barrel-shaped gym-bag silhouette - on a wooden floor in warm window light.
bags.rect_reason: Crops off the Eames chair that owns the right half of the frame.
bags.deviation: The brief asked for a sports/gym holdall in an athletic style. Every athletic holdall in the free pool carried a maker's mark across the side, so this logo-free canvas holdall is a deliberate substitution.

caps.shows: A completely blank trucker cap - white front panel, charcoal mesh sides, black brim - on a plain pale grey ground. No crest, no wordmark, no text.
caps.deviation: The brief asked for a stack or flat-lay of caps. Every stack and flat-lay found on Unsplash and Pexels carried a legible third-party brand (Nike, New Balance, Ralph Lauren, LA Dodgers, Titleist, NBA teams, AC/DC, a national coat of arms, or a 'HYDRO / PREMIUM HEADWEAR' sticker on every brim). One apparent stack turned out to be woven table mats. A single blank cap was shipped instead: the no-logo rule is absolute, the composition note is not.

belts.shows: A single tan leather belt with a plain pin buckle, worn over blue trousers under an untucked white shirt, cropped tight at the waist.
belts.note: NEW SLOT - did not exist in CIRCLE_ART before this round.

scarves.shows: An oversized camel-and-brown check mohair scarf wound high over a white shirt, against a dark doorway. Styled on a person, warm - not a folded flat grey stack.
scarves.note: NEW SLOT - did not exist in CIRCLE_ART before this round.

type_tiles.$comment: TYPE_TILE_ART['fashion'] in apps/web/src/lib/tabArt.ts, read through typeTileArt(cat, key). The 'What are you looking for?' row, new this round, in this order: tops, sets, shirts, bags, caps, belts, scarves. All seven are 600x800 WebP - one ratio for the whole row, baked into the file rather than left to object-fit, so the row that was judged is the row that ships.
type_tiles.$brief: Same quality bar as the circles, plus one literal rule: the photograph must match its label. A shirt on Shirts, a cap on Caps. Bags / caps / belts / scarves REUSE the four accessory-circle photographs at a second, portrait crop - explicitly permitted, and worth more than novelty here because those four were already opened at full size and cleared of brand marks on an earlier round (a cap search is a minefield of embroidered logos). They are separate storage objects under art/type/, not shared files: a 600x800 tile cannot share an object with a 400x400 circle.

tops.shows: A washed brown oversized t-shirt over black trousers, on a woman seated on white seamless, with a gold pendant. The t-shirt fills the tile.
tops.rect_reason: The uncropped frame is a whole seated figure and the t-shirt is a detail in the middle of it - it read as 'an outfit', not 'a top'. This box crops in on the tee.
tops.note: Same shoot (photo-1780566xxxxx) as art/hero/fashion-3.jpg, which is a different frame and is not currently rendered - HERO_ART['fashion'] points at art/hero/fashion-cedar-street.jpg. Different image, so not a duplicate, but worth knowing before either is changed.

sets.shows: A light blue two-piece - cropped blazer and matching high-waisted belted trousers - worn head to toe with blue suede heeled sandals, on a cream seamless. A vase of dried grasses stands at her feet.
sets.rect_reason: The only tile that has to say 'these two pieces match', so it keeps the whole figure instead of cropping in.
sets.checked: The vase and dried grasses are a plain studio prop with no lettering on them.

shirts.shows: A crisp white button-up shirt - collar, placket, buttons and shoulder - on a man against a warm sand ground, cropped just above the mouth. No lettering anywhere on the garment.
shirts.rect_reason: The source is a 6720x4480 landscape frame with the shirt right of centre; this takes the right-hand 3360px, which is the full height and the shirt.

bags.shows: A tan canvas holdall - the barrel-shaped gym-bag silhouette - on a wooden floor in warm window light.
bags.rect_reason: Tighter than the circle's rect: at 3:4 the wider box let the Eames chair back into the frame, which is the thing the circle's rect exists to remove.

caps.shows: A completely blank trucker cap - white front panel, charcoal mesh sides, black brim - on a plain pale grey ground. No crest, no wordmark, no text.
caps.rect_reason: Centres the cap in a portrait box; the uncropped 6000x4000 frame has it small in a wide field of grey.

belts.shows: A single tan leather belt with a plain pin buckle, worn over blue trousers under an untucked white shirt, cropped tight at the waist.
belts.known_compromise: The darkest tile in the row. The belt still reads first, but if the row is ever rebalanced for light this is the one to replace.

scarves.shows: An oversized camel-and-brown check mohair scarf with a fringed end, wound over a white shirt with turned-back cuffs. THE HEAD IS CROPPED OUT: the scarf fills the tile.
scarves.rect_reason: The circle's crop of this photograph includes the model's face against a dark brick doorway, which at tile size reads as a portrait with a scarf in it rather than as a scarf. Starting below the chin gives the frame to the garment and pushes the dark doorway into a corner.
scarves.reuse_of: art/circle/fashion--scarves.webp (same photograph, 400x400 square crop including the face)

tiles.$comment: CATEGORY_TILE_ART['fashion'] in apps/web/src/lib/tabArt.ts - the four SAVED-VIEW tiles (New in / Most gifted / Under $75 / Deals), untouched this round and listed here for provenance only. All four are 600x800 WebP - identical crop ratio, as the brief requires - and all four are editorial fashion photography: a full-length styled figure on a pale seamless studio ground, in cream / camel / white / black.

new-in.shows: Two women against white seamless in mirrored cropped blazers - cream over black trousers, black over camel trousers. The brightest of the four and the only one with two figures.

most-gifted.shows: A woman in a cream double-breasted trench, black tights and black boots, seated on a black chair in a pale grey studio with soft window light on the wall behind.

under-75.shows: A woman in an oversized white shirt, black tailored trousers and black heels on pale grey seamless - the everyday-basics look.

deals.shows: A man in a black floral-print short-sleeve shirt, black trousers and unbranded white trainers on pale grey. The one menswear frame in the row, and the darkest.
